doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Teo Macero and The Transfiguration of Hiram Brown
summary: He disliked Macero and the Rudolph idea but liked making the Hiram Brown record.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: See all the information we can extract from seemingly random clues? Is there anything we can speak about your time at Columbia, working with Teo Macero?
No, I didn’t get along with him too much. He was a classical composer. That turned me off, I think...I don’t know. But when he suggested “Rudolph The Red-Nosed Reindeer...”
He was the one who suggested that?
But the records you made for Columbia weren’t particularly commercial.
One has one of the best titles ever, The Transfiguration of Hiram Brown.
Oh, yeah. I liked that record. I made it with Jerry Segal and Addison Farmer, downtown in a big room...
Well, I don’t know. But that was Teo Macero. I remember he wanted to play on some record, and he got his saxophone out—and I didn’t let him.
He wanted to play on one of the tracks?
